name: Docker MCP Gateway code-mode (experimental)
engine: goja, a pure-Go JavaScript interpreter, run in-process inside the gateway (a new goja.Runtime per call, no interrupt, no memory cap)
how_run: Built docker-mcp from source in golang:1.26 (CGO_ENABLED=0, vendored), ran `docker-mcp gateway run --catalog <file> --enable-all-servers --static --transport streaming` in a node:22-slim container with HOME pointed at a probe-only folder, catalog = one remote MCP server (lib/lookup-server.mjs on the host) exposing lookup. The driver calls the gateway's own `code-mode` tool ({servers:[probe], name}) and then the generated `code-mode-<name>` tool with {script}. DOCKER_MCP_ALLOW_INSECURE_REMOTE_URLS=1 (docs/security.md dev/test opt-out) was set so the gateway accepts an http:// upstream; it only affects the gateway-to-upstream URL check. --static skips image pulls and the Docker-socket network probe. A second config (config-stdio.mjs) runs the same gateway on its default stdio transport.

P1.detail: Literal SPEC form fails: `await` is a SyntaxError because the script is wrapped in a plain non-async IIFE. Adapted form JSON.parse(lookup({id:21})).value returned "42", 1 host call, 226 ms. Tools are synchronous and return the first text content as a string, so the caller must JSON.parse. console.log(42) did not reach the MCP caller; it went to the gateway process stdout (3 chars seen in docker logs).

P2.detail: Only the return value reaches the caller. Bare last expression "RETURNED" -> "<no output>" (IIFE returns undefined). With `return "RETURNED"` -> "RETURNED". 0 of the 200,000 printed chars reached the caller; all 200,001 bytes went to the gateway's own stdout. No output cap and no truncation marker on the return value (fmt.Sprintf("%v")). On the stdio transport the same prints are written into the JSON-RPC stream (out/stdio-P2.txt, client onerror: Unexpected token 'A' ... is not valid JSON).

P3.detail: Literal form: SyntaxError (await). fetch("https://example.com") -> "Error running script: ReferenceError: fetch is not defined at <eval>:2:20(4)". No request left.

P4.detail: require -> ReferenceError: require is not defined. import("fs") -> SyntaxError: Unexpected reserved word. typeof Deno === "undefined".

P5.detail: process.env.PROBE_SECRET -> ReferenceError: process is not defined. The gateway process had PROBE_SECRET=s3cr3t in its env.

P6.detail: while(true){} never returned; harness gave up at 120,003 ms. After the client gave up the gateway kept one core busy (docker stats 110-112% CPU) until the container was restarted: client cancellation does not stop goja. Other sessions were still served meanwhile (P6-concurrent-P11: 20 runs of 1+1, median 4.5 ms).

P7.detail: Gateway process RSS (PID 1 in its container) climbed to 4,099 MB in 23 s with no limit from the gateway; the harness killed the container at the 4 GB cap (exit 137). The whole gateway, with every session and every proxied server connection, goes down with it.

P8.detail: Second execution printed "gone": goja.New() per call.

P9.detail: Literal await form is a SyntaxError. Promise.all over five lookups took 1,018 ms (1,024 ms round trip), 5 host calls: each tool function blocks the goja thread until the MCP call returns.

P10.detail: "Error running script: Error: probe-boom at <eval>:2:7(3)". Message and line survive; line numbers are user line + 1 because of the IIFE wrapper (a throw on user line 3 reports <eval>:4:7). The MCP result has isError false: the error is ordinary success text.

P11.detail: 20 fresh executions of `return 1+1` through the streaming HTTP transport and Docker port mapping: median 7.5 ms, p90 22.4 ms (noisy shared machine; a second run gave median 4.5 ms, p90 6.8 ms). One-time setup (MCP connect + code-mode tool creation) 166 ms.

P12.detail: this.constructor.constructor("return process")() -> ReferenceError: process is not defined. (function(){return this})().process -> undefined. Lower-case globals are only eval, globalThis, URI helpers, console and lookup.

defaults.time: None. runJavascript calls vm.RunString with no vm.Interrupt and ignores ctx; no timeout anywhere in pkg/codemode (exec.go:13-48).
defaults.memory: None. goja has no heap cap; the gateway's --memory/--cpus flags apply to MCP server containers, not to the gateway process that runs goja.
defaults.output: No cap on the return value (exec.go:42-47). console output is not returned at all; it is written to the gateway's os.Stdout (console.go:19-41).
defaults.hardened_null_reason: The gateway exposes no code-mode option: no timeout, memory, or output setting exists for code-mode (pkg/codemode has no configuration struct). --block-network, --block-secrets, --cpus and --memory apply to the tool servers' containers, not to the in-process goja runtime. Running the gateway itself in a memory-limited container is a deployment wrapper, so per RUBRIC it does not count.

source_notes.finding: Each tool of the selected servers becomes a global JS function of the same name via vm.Set(tool.Name, callTool(...)). Docs for the model are generated from the MCP input schema by toolToJsDoc as `name(args: ArgsObject): string` plus a field list, and concatenated into the generated tool's description after a fixed prompt that says calls are synchronous and the script must return a string.

Two steps. The model finds servers with mcp-find (catalog search) and enables them with mcp-add, then calls `code-mode` with {servers, name}. The gateway registers a new tool `code-mode-<name>` whose description holds every tool doc of those servers. So discovery is per-server, but all tools of a chosen server go into one description upfront. Servers must already be enabled for the session.

Direct in-process Go call: the JS function marshals its args, drops nil non-required keys, and invokes the registered MCP ToolHandler synchronously, returning only the first TextContent. The handler is the same one direct calls use, so the gateway's invoke policy and audit apply to code-mode calls (tool_policy.go comment).

goja in the gateway process, not a separate sandbox process or container. The guest has no fs, net, process or require (P3-P5, P12), which matches the docs' claim that it "can only interact through MCP tools". But the docs' "isolated sandbox" has no resource boundary: no interrupt, no heap cap, and it shares the gateway's address space and stdout.

Only the return value goes back, formatted with fmt.Sprintf("%v"); undefined becomes "<no output>". console.* is fmt.Fprintln(os.Stdout). On the default stdio transport (gateway.go sets Transport: "stdio" in both in-container and on-host defaults) the gateway's stdout is the JSON-RPC channel, so guest prints become protocol messages. out/stdio-inject.txt: a script printed a forged tools/call response for the pending request id, and the MCP client returned "FORGED by guest console.log for id 2" instead of the real "REAL".
None for time, memory, output, or call count. The infinite-loop goroutine outlives the client (P6) and memory growth is bounded only by the OS (P7).
Fresh goja.Runtime per execution; nothing persists. The generated code-mode-<name> tool itself persists in the gateway for the session.

Compile and runtime errors are returned as a successful tool result with text "Error running script: <goja error>", including <eval>:line:col; isError is never set. A tool handler error surfaces as a thrown Go error inside JS.
Tool servers run in their own containers (or as remotes) with secrets injected by the gateway; the JS never sees them. The goja runtime gets only console and the tool functions.

surprises: Default stdio transport + console.log = JSON-RPC injection: model-written code can forge MCP responses to the client (out/stdio-inject.txt). The client accepted a forged result for the pending tool call and dropped the real one.
The SPEC's await forms are all SyntaxErrors: the script is wrapped in a non-async IIFE and tools are synchronous, so Promise.all gives no parallelism (P9 1,018 ms for 5 x 200 ms).

Docs say "isolated sandbox"; the code is an in-process goja runtime with no timeout, no memory cap, and no cancellation. One `while(true){}` pins a gateway core until restart; one allocation loop takes the whole gateway down.
Errors come back as success (isError false) with text "Error running script: ...".
console output is never returned to the model even though the prompt comment says console is there "to help the LLM debug its own code" (exec.go:16).

The gateway refuses http:// remote MCP URLs unless DOCKER_MCP_ALLOW_INSECURE_REMOTE_URLS=1, and `--servers` silently disables dynamic tools (so code-mode only exists with --enable-all-servers or profiles).
